_comment: Segment binding at the peasant seam — bestiary.Resolve(ref, WithInputFormat(InputFormatPeasant)), which is exactly what `bestiary show <ref>` passes. The corpus is driven HERE and not at a bare Resolve() on purpose: five of the six must-not-widen refs below are NOTFOUND at a bare Resolve() (auto-detect routes them to SchemeHuggingFace/SchemeRaw), so pinning them there would pin NOTFOUND->NOTFOUND and be vacuous. Each row pins its CANDIDATE SET, not merely its outcome class: `entities` is the sorted set of entity keys the candidate set spans (the identity-level candidate set, the granularity the acceptance criterion is written in), and `refs` is the sorted provider|id set, pinned for the must-not-widen rows where provider-level widening is the risk and deliberately left empty elsewhere. Roles: `repair` = a ref the fallback pass newly answers (was model-not-found before the segment-binding repair); `must-not-widen` = a ref that already resolved in the strict pass and must come back byte-identical, since a widened binding here is how a positional-parser repair silently breaks working lookups; `entity-view-guard` = a live entity key that must stay model-not-found at this seam, because `show` only reaches its aggregate entity view when model resolution misses — letting the fallback pass claim these keys is how a resolver-only sweep can hide a large CLI regression; `deferred-witness` = a documented slot, see its own mutation note.

provenance.ref: the amended unique-resolution arm of the segment-binding criterion: `ling/2.6` resolves uniquely to `ling@2.6#1t`

mutation.description: two segments, no provider prefix: the trailing version token lands in the VARIANT slot under positional binding and can never match a variant-empty entity, so the ref was unresolvable before the repair

provenance.ref: the same criterion's provider-qualified spelling: `ant/ling/2.6` resolves uniquely to `ling@2.6#1t`

mutation.description: the provider prefix is consumed by the pre-existing three-segment strip arm, leaving the same two-segment residue as the bare spelling — so both spellings must land on the same single identity, and the variant-carrying siblings at that same version must NOT be pulled in

provenance.ref: the criterion's scoped-ambiguity arm: `openai/gpt@5.1` returns ErrAmbiguous over exactly its openai-served candidates

mutation.description: the two-segment provider strip is guarded on the candidate's OWN Provider field, so the ambiguity is scoped to the named provider instead of every host of the family; an is-a-known-provider test would not do, since mistral/minimax/meta/google/openai are all known providers AND family-shaped tokens

provenance.ref: the criterion's `gpt/5.1` arm: an improvement from not-found to a correctly-scoped ambiguity over its groups, NOT a unique resolution

mutation.description: no provider segment, so no strip fires and the ambiguity spans every host of the family — the row exists to pin that the repair does not silently narrow an honestly-ambiguous ref to one provider

provenance.ref: the criterion's `openai/gpt/5.1` arm, over its groups

mutation.description: the three-segment strip arm carries no provider-equality guard (unchanged by this repair), so this spelling stays as wide as the bare one — pinned so a later tightening of that arm cannot land unnoticed

provenance.ref: the worked example behind the if/else form of the variant-empty version binding: an abort form loses thousands of resolvable refs of this shape

mutation.description: an explicitly named variant plus an @-suffix that is a VERSION rather than a date: the variant slot is already pinned, so the date-to-version rebind applies unconditionally here — a rebind rule that refused variant-carrying candidates outright would drop this ref

provenance.ref: the structural twin, verifiable today, of the deferred composition witness: a family+version whose artifacts are ALL variant-carrying resolves to a correctly-scoped ambiguity over those tier keys, not to not-found

mutation.description: the catalog holds no variant-empty `claude@4.6`, so the base-first preference finds nothing and the last-resort pass lets the rebound version segment reach the variant-carrying tiers; the ling rows above are the control that this pass never fires when a variant-empty artifact DOES exist

provenance.ref: known falsifier: a catalog id that IS literally `<vendor>/<family>`, the exact shape the two-segment provider strip could mis-read

mutation.description: resolves in the strict pass as an exact model id, so no repair rule may run at all — a rule that fired per-model rather than on a globally empty match set would widen this to every codestral host

provenance.ref: known falsifier: a vendor-prefixed catalog id served by four providers, where a widened binding would add rows from the bare-`sonar` family

mutation.description: the multi-provider case of the same shape: the pinned ref set is the whole point, since a widening here changes WHICH rows come back without changing the entity key

provenance.ref: known falsifier: a family/variant ref that is ALSO a live entity key, so a widening would cost the key its `show` entity view as well as its model view

mutation.description: family plus a real variant, no version anywhere: the variant-empty rebind must not fire because the strict pass already answered

provenance.ref: known falsifier: a family/variant ref whose single row carries a vendor-prefixed id unrelated to the ref's own segments

mutation.description: the ref's segments and the resolved id share no prefix, so a binding change shows up as a different id rather than a different provider

provenance.ref: known falsifier: a family whose own name ENDS in a version-shaped token, the hardest case for any rule that re-reads a segment as a version

mutation.description: the digit `3` sits inside the family segment rather than in a slot of its own — a rebind rule that scanned for version-shaped tokens instead of using slot position would mangle this ref

provenance.ref: known falsifier: a hyphenated family whose LEADING token is also a live provider name (`xpersona`), the trap the two-segment provider strip is guarded against

mutation.description: the family segment begins with a provider name but is not equal to one, so the provider-equality guard must leave it alone; a prefix-based strip would delete `xpersona-` and lose the ref

provenance.ref: a pinned member of the entity-view set the criterion protects: `show llama@3.3#70b` must keep rendering its aggregate entity view

mutation.description: a bare, sized entity key with an @-suffix that is a version, not a date: this is exactly the shape an ungated date-to-version rebind swallows into model resolution, which silently costs the key its entity view — the rebind is gated on a provider segment having been stripped, and this key has none

provenance.ref: a pinned member of the protected entity-view set

mutation.description: the unsized, variant-empty spelling of the same trap: family plus an @-version and nothing else

provenance.ref: a pinned member of the protected entity-view set

mutation.description: the variant-carrying spelling: two segments plus an @-version, so both the variant-empty rebind and the date-to-version rebind must decline it

provenance.ref: a pinned member of the protected entity-view set

mutation.description: the identity-modifier spelling: the `{...}` segment is stripped before slot binding, so this key exercises the same trap with a modifier attached

provenance.ref: the composition witness of the segment-binding criterion, held open here: it passes only once the gpt tier re-key has ALSO landed, and this row records the state before that lever

mutation.description: DOCUMENTED SLOT — do not read this row as a claim that a base `gpt@5.6` artifact exists; it is measured that none does and that no upstream row would produce one. Until the tier re-key lands, the 5.6 tiers are not variants of family `gpt`, so this ref names nothing. The slice that re-keys them REPLACES this row with a must-pass ambiguity over the three resulting tier keys; the `claude/4.6` row above is its structural twin and already proves the binding half of the composition.
